source_text: Πλὴν καὶ ἄκων ἐνέπεσεν ὁ Κέλσος εἰς τὸ μαρτυρεῖν τῷ νεώτερον εἶναι τὸν κόσμον καὶ οὐδέπω μυρίων ἐτῶν εἰπὼν καὶ Ἕλληνας ταῦτα νομίζειν ἀρχαῖα, ὡς πρεσβύτερα διὰ τοὺς κατακλυσμοὺς καὶ τὰς ἐκπυρώσεις οὐ τεθεωρήκασιν οὐδ᾿ ἀπομνημονεύουσιν. ἔστωσαν δὲ τῷ Κέλσῳ τοῦ περὶ τῶν ἐκπυρώσεων καὶ ἐξυδατώσεων μύθου διδάσκαλοι οἱ κατ᾿ αὐτὸν σοφώτατοι Αἰγύπτιοι, ὧν τῆς σοφίας ἴχνη ἄλογα ζῷα προσκυνούμενα καὶ λόγοι παριστάντες εὔλογον εἶναι καὶ ἀνακεχωρηκυῖάν τινα καὶ μυστικὴν τὴν τοιαύτην τοῦ θεοῦ θεραπείαν. κἂν μὲν Αἰγύπτιοι περὶ τῶν ζῴων σεμνύνοντες ἑαυτῶν τὸν λόγον θεολογίας φέρωσι, σοφοί εἰσιν· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ τῷ Ἰουδαίων συγκαταθέμενος νόμῳ καὶ νομοθέτῃ πάντα ἀναφέρῃ ἐπὶ τὸν τῶν ὅλων δημιουργὸν μόνον θεὸν. ἥττων εἶναι παρὰ Κέλσῳ καὶ τοῖς ὁμοίοις αὐτῷ λογίζεται τοῦ μὴ εἰς λογικὰ μόνον καὶ θνητὰ ζῷα ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰς ἄλογα κατάγοντος τὴν θεότητα ὑπὲρ τὴν μυθικὴν μετενσωμάτωσιν. τὴν περὶ τῆς πιπτούσης ἀπὸ τῶν ἁψίδων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ψυχῆς καὶ ἕως τῶν ἀλόγων ζῴων, οὐ μόνον ἡμέρων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀγριωτάτων. καταβαινούσης. καὶ ἐὰν μὲν Αἰγύπτιοι μυθολογῶσι, πιστεύονται πεφιλοσοφηκέναι δι᾿ αἰνιγμῶν καὶ ἀποῤῥήτων, ἐὰν δὲ Μω(??)σῆς ὅλῳ ἔθνει συγγράφων ἱστορίας καὶ νόμους αὐτοῖς καταλίπῃ. μῦθοι κενοὶ νομίζονται μηδ᾿ ἀλληγορίαν ἐπιδεχόμενοι οἱ λόγοι αὐτοῦ·
pass_a_gloss: But also Celsus unwillingly fell into testifying that the world is younger and not yet ten thousand years old, saying that Greeks also think these things are ancient, as they have not observed nor remembered older things because of the floods and conflagrations. Let the most wise Egyptians, according to him, be the teachers of the myth about conflagrations and inundations, whose wisdom is indicated by irrational animals being worshiped and words presenting a logical argument, and having retreated to some mystical service of God. And if indeed Egyptians, honoring animals, bring their reasoning to a theological level, they are wise; but if the one who lays down the law with the Jews and the lawgiver refers everything to the one God, the creator of all. He is considered inferior by Celsus and those like him because he does not lead divinity only to rational and mortal animals, but also to irrational ones, beyond the mythical transmigration. The thing about the soul falling from the vaults of heaven, and going down as far as irrational animals, not only tame but also wild, is considered to be going down. And if Egyptians mythologize, they are believed to have philosophized through riddles and arcane sayings; but if Moses, writing history and laws for the whole nation, leaves them behind, his words are considered empty myths, not admitting allegory.

choices.why: indicates Celsus did not intend to testify
indicates the reason for the judgment
indicates the action of the subject

pass_b_english: Celsus even falls into testifying against his will that the world is younger and not yet ten thousand years old, saying that Greeks also think these things are ancient because they have neither observed nor remembered older things, on account of the floods and conflagrations. (Let the most wise Egyptians, according to him, be the teachers of the myth about conflagrations and inundations, whose wisdom is shown by irrational animals being worshiped and words that present a logical argument, having retreated to some mystical and withdrawn service of God.) And if indeed Egyptians, honoring their animals, bring their reasoning to a theological level, they are wise; but if the one who agrees with the Jewish law and lawgiver refers everything to the one God, the creator of all, he is considered inferior by Celsus and those like him, on the grounds that he does not bring the divinity down only to rational and mortal animals but also to irrational ones, beyond the mythical transmigration. The matter of the soul falling from the vaults of heaven and descending as far as irrational animals, not only tame but also wild, is a descent. And if Egyptians mythologize, they are believed to have philosophized through riddles and arcane sayings; but if Moses, writing history and laws for the whole nation, leaves them behind, his words are considered empty myths that do not even admit allegory.
